s1.syndrome_frame: Prolonged febrile illness with systemic symptoms and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Pancytopenia with low hemoglobin, leukocyte, and platelet counts
Elevated liver transaminases and ferritin levels
key_facts: 65-year-old male patient
Presenting with high-grade fever, nausea, vomiting, and generalized weakness for 10 days
History of intermittent high-grade fever, vomiting, loss of weight, and night sweats for one month
Medical history of hypertension and benign prostate hyperplasia
Temperature of 101°F
Mild hepatosplenomegaly and conjunctival pallor on physical examination
Laboratory tests showed pancytopenia, elevated liver transaminases, and high ferritin levels
Negative serology for hepatitis B/C, HIV, malaria, dengue, and scrub typhus
Negative blood, urine, and sputum cultures
Imaging studies showed hepatosplenomegaly, fatty liver, and mild urinary bladder wall thickening
Bone marrow biopsy showed erythroid hyperplasia with megaloblastic erythropoiesis and erythroid and lymphophagocytosis
Molecular testing detected MTB with Rifampicin indeterminate
